proposals.title: Keep the paid-API base-address rule in REQ-SAG-0019; delete the copy in REQ-SAG-0801

changes.before: Configuration MUST NOT change where a paid API's key is sent.

proposals.justification: REQ-SAG-0019 states 'Configuration MUST NOT change a paid API's base address.' REQ-SAG-0801 states 'Configuration MUST NOT change where a paid API's key is sent.' In REQ-SAG-0019's definitions a paid API's key is sent only to that provider's built-in base address, so the two statements are the same obligation (Jev: duplicate, 0.86). Under 'Correcting duplicates' rule 4, between two REQs the statement stays in the record whose title and subject it belongs to. REQ-SAG-0019 ('Configuration file locations and lookup order') governs what configuration may and may not set, including model entries. It is also the record that already carries the matching acceptance criterion, 'a model entry whose provider is not a built-in provider fails the load with a typed error'. REQ-SAG-0801 ('Local decision runners come from configuration') is about local runners, and a paid API is not a local runner. This is a deletion with no rewording, so the kept statement is untouched. REQ-SAG-0801 keeps seven statements, so it is not left empty. Left for the lead and not proposed here: REQ-SAG-0801's 'paid API' definition and its last acceptance criterion (the key is still sent only to the built-in endpoint) now back a statement that lives in REQ-SAG-0019. Neither is a statement, so they are outside this duplicate, but the lead may want them handled in the same pass.
proposals.improvement: One copy of the paid-API rule, in REQ-SAG-0019. REQ-SAG-0801 drops from 8 to 7 statements and no longer restates a configuration rule.

proposals.title: Cut the fixed `decider` resolution from REQ-SAG-0801 so it does not pin a model version against ANC-001

changes.before: A selection of `decider` MUST resolve to the 4b decider model.

proposals.justification: ANC-001 makes the decidr Jev selection follow the newest Jev model in the table, with config as the only override. This statement fixes a selection to the single `decider-4b-v2.1` row, so the table's newest-first ordering cannot decide it. Jev rates the cell as a conflict (P(conflicts) 0.74). The statement is also the only one that names the pinned row, so cutting it removes the conflict. Unclear point: the trace does not show whether the owner means `decider` as a separate pinned alias outside ANC-001's `jev` name. If so, the owner should reject this proposal and state that as an anchor. The definition sentence 'The 4b decider model is the `decider-4b-v2.1` row' in the requirement text would then be unused. Definitions are not statements, so this proposal does not touch it. I could not read the code to check this; the tools I could use for that were unavailable.

source.quote: I want 'jev' to select latest, config can override default.

proposals.improvement: REQ-SAG-0801 no longer fixes a selection to one model version. Resolution follows the model table's newest-row rule (REQ-SAG-0102) and config. One statement fewer, no wording added.

proposals.title: Cut the fixed-model-id requirement for local runners from REQ-SAG-0801

changes.before: Each local decision runner's model MUST have a fixed model id in the model table.

proposals.justification: ANC-009 requires only that the model table accept extra rows from config. This statement adds a structural constraint on the rows of local runners. Every table row already has a fixed model id by definition (REQ-SAG-0102 defines a row as having one). Jev's reading of the cell is that obligations on this topic go beyond the anchor (P(exceeds) 0.85). The statement duplicates the row definition and goes past the anchor, so at the aggressive level it is deleted. 'Configuration MUST be able to add a local model that runs on another computer' stays: it serves ANC-009 (P(serves) 0.82).

proposals.title: Cut the log-retention statements from REQ-SAG-0003 unless the owner anchors them

changes.before: A session log MUST remain in `~/.sc-agent/sessions/` whatever its age.
A run log MUST remain in `~/.sc-agent/sessions/` whatever its age.
sc-agent MUST NOT contain code that removes a general log.
sc-agent MUST NOT remove a session log.
sc-agent MUST NOT remove a run log.

proposals.justification: ANC-005 asks only that default loggers write under the configured log root with a fixed folder and file name. It says nothing about keeping or removing logs. These five statements are a retention policy that no anchor states, so at aggressive level they are deleted until the owner anchors them. I believe the policy is needed: the record's rationale says session logs are the long-term record used to analyse tens of thousands of decisions, and losing one loses data. I therefore also propose the anchor below. ANC-015 and ANC-016 do not cover logging retention either, so this cut is the only unanchored behaviour I found in the record. I could not tie the ANC-015 and ANC-016 yellow cells to any other statement and list them here as cleared by this cut. The owner should check that.

source.quote: I mandated - that all default loggers created in production have root/folder/file naming conventions specified.

proposals.improvement: REQ-SAG-0003 drops from 9 to 4 statements and states only log placement and the log-root override. The retention rule returns only if the owner anchors it.
proposals.proposed_anchor: sc-agent must never remove, rotate or prune a general log, a session log or a run log, whatever its age, so the long-term record of decisions is never lost.

proposals.title: Cut the wheel packaging constraint from REQ-SAG-0008

changes.before: The wheel MUST NOT depend on the `sc-observability` Python package.

proposals.justification: ANC-005 covers where default loggers write, and ANC-016 covers defining the injection path and keeping derivative tools off it in production. A prohibition on a Python package dependency is a packaging constraint that neither anchor states. The other two statements stay: injection of a general Logger (ANC-016) and a named Logger built from the linked crate (ANC-005 default loggers). If the owner wants the no-package choice kept, it is a choice between alternatives and belongs in an ADR (ADR-SAG-0019 is already related to this record).

source.quote: judge-jev/plan-anchor and other derivative tools should defer to the default tool rules and not use injection path for production code (test only).

proposals.improvement: REQ-SAG-0008 drops from 3 to 2 statements and states only the logger injection and acquisition behaviour the anchors cover.

proposals.title: Cut the paid-API base-address prohibition from REQ-SAG-0019 unless the owner anchors it

changes.before: Configuration MUST NOT change a paid API's base address.

proposals.justification: ANC-001 requires `jev` to select the newest Jev model with a config default override. ANC-009 requires that config can add model rows. Neither limits what configuration may set, so a prohibition on changing a paid API's base address is a stricter constraint than either anchor and is deleted at aggressive level. I believe it is needed: the record's definitions and rationale say a paid API's key is sent only to that provider's built-in address, and configuration must not redirect that key. I therefore propose the anchor below. The unit test on a model entry whose provider is not built in is acceptance-criterion text and goes with whatever the owner decides.

proposals.proposed_anchor: Configuration must not change the base address of a paid API, so an API key is sent only to that provider's built-in endpoint.

This depends on REQ-SAG-0801 keeping that statement. REQ-SAG-0801 is outside my slice and I did not check whether another proposal changes it.

proposals.title: Delete REQ-SAG-0101 (model short names)
proposals.justification: Both statements go beyond ANC-001 and ANC-009. ANC-001 constrains only the `jev` alias, and ANC-009 constrains only config-added rows. Resolving every cloud short name and every local short name is outside both. Cutting the excess leaves the record with no statements, so it is deleted. The resolution of short names is already stated in REQ-SAG-0102 (a short name resolves to its newest row) and in REQ-SAG-0801 (`decider` resolves to the 4b row, and local runners are selectable by name). REQ-SAG-0102 lists REQ-SAG-0101 under `dependencies.related`; that link must be dropped when the record is deleted.

changes.before: The built-in rows of the model table MUST be sorted by release date, newest first.

proposals.justification: ANC-001 requires only that `jev` selects the newest Jev model. It does not require a sort order for the table. The statement that a short name resolves to its newest row stays, and so does the requirement that each built-in model carries its published release date, which is how 'newest' is decided. ANC-009 does not ask for a sort order either.

proposals.title: Cut the no-branching-on-catalog-name rule from REQ-SAG-0102

changes.before: `sc-agent` MUST NOT branch on a catalog name.

proposals.justification: This is a code-structure prohibition. ANC-001 and ANC-009 do not ask for it, and it applies to provider names and model ids as well as the table. ANC-012 (provider dispatch) has the related constraint of no matching on wire strings outside the implementations, and any broader branching rule belongs with that anchor, not in the model-table record. Cutting it also removes the definitions (catalog name, branch on) from use, so the owner may want to drop those definition sentences in the same edit.
